transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Authorities in Spain say at least 10 people have been killed in a high-speed train collision today.
One train apparently collided with a second that was stopped for unknown reasons.
Authorities fear this death toll will rise.
Last January, 45 people died in Spain when a passenger train collided with an oncoming train.
President Trump heads for Chillicothe, Ohio today to campaign for Republicans.
That includes Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy and incumbent Senator John Huston, among others.
NPR's Danielle Kurtz-Laban says Trump has been focusing on GOP-led states to motivate Republicans to vote.
The case for these rallies is simple. It's that Trump is still really, really good at energizing the base.
And the GOP base still loves him, so the theory is that there are still gettable MAGA votes to turn out.
Now all that said, it is still true Trump is showing up in red states to do this.
So if he needs, and that's if, to get extra votes in a red state, that still signals a problem for his party.
NPR's Danielle Kurtz-Laban reporting.
The Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged today.
But as NPR's Scott Horsley reports, that doesn't mean inflation has been contained.
Prices are still climbing faster than the Federal Reserve would like,
and faster than average wages, putting the squeeze on workers' buying power.
The war with Iran has triggered a spike in energy prices,
while the artificial intelligence boom is raising the cost of construction materials and electronic equipment.
Nevertheless, investors think the Fed will likely hold its benchmark interest rates steady
when policymakers wrap up their meeting this afternoon.
Members of the central bank's rate-setting committee have said while they're determined to tame inflation,
they can afford to take their time.
A rate hike is widely expected at the next Fed meeting in December.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The government of Democratic Republic of the Congo says that more than 10,000 people have contracted the Ebola virus during this outbreak.
NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports that about half of them have perished.
The DRC reached this grim threshold in just over five months.
For context, at this point in the largest Ebola outbreak ever, the 2014 West Africa outbreak,
only about 4,000 people were infected.
That trajectory makes this current outbreak the fastest spreading ever.
A number of factors have fueled this rapid spread.
For one, the virus was spreading undetected for months before officials declared the outbreak.
It's also spreading in remote parts of DRC, making the response harder.
Officials have made some progress in containing it.
Better testing, treatment, and outreach have helped rein in cases in areas where the outbreak started.
But the virus is ramping up in new parts of DRC, so case counts continue climbing.
In recent weeks, that uncontrolled spread has spilled into neighboring countries, including Kenya and Nigeria.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Results from yesterday's election in Israel remain too close to call.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party and the Israeli opposition are very close.
Neither have a clear path to victory.
Even when Israeli officials tally which party got the most votes,
it will be a while before a new prime minister is chosen.
In the U.S., more than 35 million Americans have cast early ballots for this year's midterm election,
according to the University of Florida's election lab.
From member station WRKF in Baton Rouge, Brooke Thorrington reports some Louisiana voters have cast ballots in style.
Southern University's marching band, better known as the Human Chew Fox,
sauntered to City Hall for the last day of early voting.
tuba player Kevin Wilkins describes what a second line is.
I call it a moving party. We play some music and we move to a destination.
So for this event, the destination is the polls.
It's a pretty unique first for trumpet player Christian Miller.
This is going to be my first time and my first experience.
Early voting this midterm is up 66 percent in Louisiana compared to 2022.
For NPR News, I'm Brooke Thorrington in Baton Rouge.
The Milwaukee Brewers did not sweep at the World Series last night.
The Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Brewers in Florida in four to three.
But Milwaukee leads the series three games to one.
Game five of the World Series will be tonight.
It will be at the Tampa Bay Rays home park.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
This message comes from Sony Pictures Classics, presenting the acclaimed new crime thriller,
The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, starring John Turturro.
Only in theaters October 23rd in New York and L.A., nationwide October 30th.

topics.text: Spain train collision kills at least 10 people, with fears the death toll will rise
Trump heads to Chillicothe, Ohio to campaign for Republicans including Vivek Ramaswamy
Federal Reserve expected to hold interest rates steady as inflation remains elevated
Democratic Republic of the Congo passes 10,000 Ebola cases, with about half dead
Israeli election results too close to call between Netanyahu's party and opposition
Over 35 million Americans have cast early midterm ballots, according to University of Florida lab
Southern University marching band leads a second line to Baton Rouge polls on last early voting day
Milwaukee Brewers lose Game 4 to Tampa Bay Rays but still lead World Series 3-1
